source.title: Array With Elements Not Equal to Average of Neighbors

teaching.hint: Can an easier condition based only on comparisons guarantee the arithmetic requirement?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: An element strictly above both neighbors or strictly below both cannot equal their average. A strict alternating order is therefore a sufficient construction.
solution_outline.approach: Sort the values, then swap consecutive pairs starting at sorted index one. This places larger members at odd positions and smaller members at interior even positions.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: After the swaps, every interior odd position exceeds both neighbors, and every interior even position is below both neighbors. Each original value still appears exactly once.
solution_outline.correctness: Distinct sorted values make both neighbor comparisons strict: each swapped odd position receives a later sorted value than either neighbor, and each interior even position receives an earlier one. Thus every constrained element is a strict extremum and cannot equal the average. Sorting and swapping preserve the input multiset.
solution_outline.complexity: `O(n log n)` time; the construction uses `O(1)` additional storage beyond an in-place sort, which may use `O(log n)` stack space.
solution_outline.pitfall: The distinctness promise is essential to strict extrema; merely returning the sorted array fails for arithmetic progressions.

source_fidelity_notes: Retained distinct values, endpoint exemption, any-valid-output semantics, and mathematical average; removed examples and platform indexing boilerplate.
common_wrong_turns: The distinctness promise is essential to strict extrema; merely returning the sorted array fails for arithmetic progressions.
